title: Three-dimensional Optical-resolution Photoacoustic Microscopy
protocol: Configure the optical irradiation system using a diode-pumped solid-state pulsed laser and a dye laser.
Focus the output laser beam with a condenser lens.
Pass the focused beam through a 50-μm pinhole positioned slightly away from the focus of the condenser lens for spatial filtering.
Attenuate the filtered beam using a neutral-density filter.
Couple the attenuated beam into a single-mode optical fiber.
Ensure that the fiber output fills the back aperture of the microscope objective to achieve a diffraction-limited optical focus.
Attach an ultrasonic transducer with a 50-MHz central frequency to a home-made acoustic-optical beam combiner for ultrasonic detection.
Align the ultrasonic transducer coaxially with the optical irradiation system.
Create a spherical cavity on the bottom of the combiner to produce an acoustic lens with a numerical aperture of 0.5 in water.
Ensure that the acoustic focal diameter is 43 μm at the 50-MHz central frequency.
Align the optical and acoustic foci confocally to maximize detection sensitivity.
Open an imaging window in the bottom of a Petri dish (9 cm in diameter).
Seal the imaging window with an ultrasonically and optically transparent polyethylene membrane.
Apply Ultrasonic gel between the polyethylene membrane and the object to be imaged.
Fill the Petri dish with deionized water to couple the wave from the object to the submerged OR-PAM imaging head.
Amplify the photoacoustic signal detected by the ultrasonic transducer using two cascaded amplifiers (ZFL 500LN, Mini-Circuits).
Digitize the amplified signal using a 14-bit data acquisition board at a sampling rate of 200 MS/s.
Control the 2-D raster scanning of the OR-PAM imaging head along the horizontal plane with a personal computer.
Trigger both the DAQ board and the pump laser for synchronization.
Translate the imaging head along the slow axis to form a volumetric image.
View the acquired images in either direct 3-D rendering or 2-D maximum amplitude projection (MAP) image.
Use pulse-echo ultrasound and an ultrasonic reflector to determine the position of the acoustic focal plane.
Maximize the coupling efficiency of the single-mode fiber.
Apply ultrasonic gel on top of an optically absorbing object, such as a piece of black tape.
Gently attach the object beneath the imaging window in the Petri dish filled with deionized water.
Lower the imaging head into the water and remove air bubbles trapped under the acoustic lens.
Adjust the imaging head until the photoacoustic signal of the absorbing object is from the acoustic focal plane, judging by the acoustic delay.
Adjust the vertical position (z position) of the microscope objective to maximize the amplitude of the photoacoustic signal generated from the flat object.
Adjust the horizontal positions (x and y positions) of the microscope objective until the photoacoustic signal generated from the target shows a symmetric pattern.
Repeat adjustment steps for z, x, and y positions until the photoacoustic signal is optimized in both symmetry and amplitude.
Anesthetize the animal with an intraperitoneal injection of a cocktail containing 1 ml ketamine (100 mg/ml), 0.1 ml xylazine (100 mg/ml), and 8.9 ml saline; dosage: 0.1 ml/10 g.
Shave the hair in the mouse ear.
Depilate residual hair with Surgi Cream before cleaning it with deionized water.
Turn on the photoacoustic laser system.
Check the system alignment.
Anesthetize the mouse with 3% isoflurane vaporized by inhalation gas, maintaining anesthesia with 1% isoflurane throughout the experiment.
Transfer the mouse to a stereotactic stage.
Control the body temperature at 37 °C using a heating pad.
Flatten the mouse ear on a plastic plate.
Apply a layer of ultrasound gel on top of the ear, avoiding air bubbles inside the gel.
Place the ear under the imaging window.
Slowly raise the animal stage until the ultrasound gel contacts the bottom of the polyethylene membrane.
Clamp a pulse oximeter to the mouse leg or tail to monitor its physiological status.
Apply ointment to the eyes to prevent dryness and accidental laser damage to the mouse eyes.
Lower the imaging head until the acoustic lens is immersed in deionized water.
Remove air bubbles trapped under the acoustic lens.
Check the laser fluence to ensure it does not exceed 20 mJ/cm².
Set the laser to the external-trigger mode and start trial scanning.
Adjust the z position of the imaging head until the strongest photoacoustic signal is from the acoustic focal plane.
Set correct scanning parameters and start formal image acquisition.
Turn off the laser.
Lift the imaging head out of the deionized water.
Lower the animal stage to release the mouse.
Clean the mouse ear with deionized water.
Turn off the anesthesia system.
Turn off the temperature controller.
Unload the mouse from the stereotactic stage.
Place the mouse in an incubator set at 37 °C if repetitive imaging is required.
Return the mouse to the animal facility after it wakes up naturally.
Euthanatize and dispose of the mouse according to animal protocols if not needed for further use.
